nodes.label: seed: evo2 prompt, Argon thinking high, merge only
nodes.change: seed: evo2 prompt, Argon thinking high, merge only

Post-processing only, no new model calls: merge window 0.4 s -> 1.2 s, and a merge now also needs the same team (same type + same team = one touch; keep the copy furthest from its clip's edge). After merging, add +0.6 s to every serve time.
Scout watch calls use thinking='medium' instead of 'high'. Same model (Argon), 5 fps, high media, prompt and merge unchanged. Settings are pulled out into the FPS/MEDIA/THINKING/MODEL constants.

New stages after merge: (1) one_serve_per_rally drops a serve within 4 s of the previous serve (keeps the copy furthest from its clip edge). (2) check_serves: for each serve, watch_range(t-1.5, t+3.5) at 10 fps with Argon thinking medium, asking for contact time (or, if the server is off-frame, the first frame the served ball appears) and the server's number only if the server is visible. Time is replaced only if within [t-0.5, t+2.5]; number only if the server is visible. Nothing is deleted by the check.

New stage fix_numbers after merge. The team sheet (match.team_sheet) is parsed into each side's regular numbers (the list before the first ';'; 'also seen once' numbers are left out). For each event whose number is null or not on its team's list, watch_range(t-1.0, t+1.5) at 10 fps, cropped to that team's half of the court plus the net zone (1120x1080, no downscale), Argon thinking medium, asks for the shirt number of the player making that touch, chosen from the team's list or null. The answer replaces the number only if it is on the list. Times, types and teams are not changed and nothing is deleted.

New find_rallies(): Flash watches each clip (fps 2, media low, thinking low, RALLIES schema) and returns rally start/end spans. windows(): pad spans by -3.5/+4.0 s, join spans closer than 4 s, widen windows shorter than 8 s, split long spans into equal chunks of at most 20 s with 6 s overlap (no short leftover piece that has no serve for context). scout() runs Argon on each window through watch_range (5 fps, media high, thinking high, default width 1280, unchanged evo2 prompt and EVENTS schema). still_playing(): if a window's last event is not a kill/block/point/error, comes within 7 s of the window's end, and no other window carries on, it watches a further 14 s window (overlap 6 s), at most twice. Merge (1.2 s, same type and team, keep the copy furthest from the window edge) and the +0.6 s serve shift are unchanged.

New stage after merge + serve lag: verify_number() runs watch_range(t-1.5, t+1.5, crop=touching team's half, width full-res, fps=10, Argon thinking medium) for every event. The number is replaced only if the reader says readable, gives digits, and the number is on that team's team-sheet line (any number accepted if the line cannot be parsed). Times, types, teams and the event list are unchanged. Errors other than BudgetExceeded keep the old number.

New post-processing stage drop_phantom_rallies after fix_numbers, with no new model calls: events are grouped into rallies (split where the gap between touches is more than 5 s), and a rally of 3 or more events in which no event has a shirt number is dropped. Rallies of 1-2 events (aces, serve errors) are always kept. The scout, merge, number re-read and serve lag are unchanged.

New live_clips() stage before the scout: Flash watches each whole clip (fps 2, media low, thinking low) with a yes/no 'is any point of the match being played at any moment (serve or rally in progress, including one already under way or starting near the end)' prompt that lists breaks, timeouts, set breaks and warm-up/practice drills as false. Only clips answered live go to the unchanged Argon scout. A missing or failed answer keeps the clip. Kept clips use exactly the same Argon calls, so their answers are cache hits and identical. Merge, serve lag and fix_numbers are unchanged.

New stage gate_rallies between merge and fix_numbers. Merged events are grouped into rallies (a new group starts after a gap > 8 s). Each group with >= 3 touches gets one watch_range over [first-2 s, last+2 s] (max 20 s), Argon thinking medium, 2 fps, low media, width 960, which labels it match_rally / warmup / no_play (an ace or service error counts as a match rally; any real rally in the cut -> match_rally). The group is dropped only if the label is not match_rally; errors, missing answers and groups of 1-2 touches are kept. Probed on all of set 1 (980-2240 s): the only group dropped is the 2218 group; all 52 real groups are kept. A first version that also gated lone serves wrongly dropped two real serves (1993, 2007), hence GATE_MIN = 3.

New stage fill_holes between merge and fix_numbers. find_holes() flags (a) consecutive touches HOLE=3.5..RALLY_END=9 s apart where the later touch is not a serve, and (b) a dig followed by a serve, by a silence of 9 s or more, or by nothing. Receive-ended rallies are not flagged because a shanked receive can end a rally. Each spot gets one watch_range: (a) from 1.5 s before to 1.5 s after the hole, or (b) from 1.5 s before the dig to 5 s after it, capped 0.5 s before the next serve. The call uses Argon thinking medium, 10 fps, full 1920 width and the EVENTS schema. The prompt lists the already-logged touches in the cut, gives the same logging rules as the scout, and asks only for missing touches. Kept: non-serve touches strictly inside the hole (more than 0.4 s from its ends), and not if the same team already has a touch within 0.7 s. New touches then go through fix_numbers like any other. Nothing is deleted or retimed. Smoke check with the threshold lowered to 1.9 s: 5 re-watches in 1140-1156, about $0.032 each, added nothing where the scout also logs nothing.

scout() no longer watches whole clips. live_clips() is unchanged (cached). The new rally_spans() asks Flash (2 fps, low media, thinking low) for each live clip's rally start/end times; a failed answer keeps the whole clip. windows() pads the spans by -3/+4 s, joins spans less than 4 s apart, widens windows to at least 8 s, and splits long rallies into 20 s windows with at least 6 s overlap. Argon then watches each window through watch_range with the same PROMPT, 5 fps, high media, thinking high and full-width frames. A window whose last touch is within 4 s of its end, and does not end the rally, gets a 14 s follow-on window (at most 2 rounds). Merge, serve lag and fix_numbers are unchanged; merge's edge margin now uses the window edges.

New stage check_numbers after fix_numbers. It covers every event whose number came from the whole-frame scout and is on its team's regular list (events already re-read by fix_numbers, and null numbers, are skipped). It runs watch_range(t-1.5, t+1.5) cropped to the team's half plus the net zone, at full resolution (1120 wide), 6 fps, Argon thinking low, with the claim, the team's numbers and a {readable, number, seen} schema. The number is replaced only if readable is true and the answer is on the team list. Times, types, teams and the event list are unchanged. Errors other than BudgetExceeded keep the old number.

New stage fill_rallies between merge and fix_numbers. broken_rallies() flags only the two rule-breaking spot types. Each spot gets one watch_range (from 1.5 s before the anchor touch to 1 s after the spot; 10 fps, full 1920 width, Argon thinking medium, EVENTS schema) with the logged touches as context. Dig-ended rallies ask for every touch after the dig until the ball is dead; attack-to-other-team spots ask only for missing touches under the scout's logging rules. Added touches must be strictly inside the spot, not serve/receive; a set is kept only if a kill follows it; and in_order() must hold: a dig/block answers the other team's attack, an attack/kill/set follows the same team's touch. Same-team duplicates within 0.7 s are dropped. Nothing is deleted or retimed; added touches go through fix_numbers.

Scout watch() calls drop from 5 to 4 fps (SCOUT_FPS = 4). Model, high media, thinking high and the prompt are unchanged. A new post-merge stage, one_touch_per_team, applies when two touches by the same team are 0.4 s apart or less: it keeps the higher-ranked type (kill > attack > block > set > dig > receive > serve) and drops the other. In set 1's current output no same-team pair is that close, so the rule only removes low-fps double logs. The live-clip gate, merge, fix_numbers (off-sheet or null numbers only) and serve lag are unchanged.

New stage serve_numbers after fix_numbers. (1) Every serve gets one watch_range from 1.5 s before to 2.5 s after the stamped serve (the 2.5 s covers an off-frame server running onto the court), cropped to the serving team's half at full resolution, 10 fps, Argon thinking medium, choosing from the team sheet or null. (2) Serves are split into serving runs (consecutive serves by the same team). In each run, on-sheet scout numbers vote 1 and zoomed reads vote 2; a clear winner goes on every serve of the run. (3) If runs 6 apart agree more often than not (so the run count lines up with the rotation), a run with no votes takes the server of the same team's runs 6, 12, ... away when those agree. A tied run takes it only if it is one of the tied numbers. Otherwise the numbers are left as they are. Times, types, teams and the event list are unchanged. I also tried a block-review stage (high-fps net-zone check of every attack->block) and dropped it: it called 3 of the 4 set-1 blocks I tested wrongly.
